sentences.text:
This revision petition under Section 397 read with Section 401 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 (for short "The Code") has been preferred by the applicant against the judgment dated 02/03/2019 passed by First Additional Sessions Judge, Jhabua, in Cri.
Appeal No.166/2016

, 
wherein the learned Judge has dismissed the appeal by affirming the conviction and sentence passed by Judicial Magistrate First Class, Jhabua vide judgment dated 14/10/2016 passed in Criminal Case No.920/2010 whereby the applicant has been convicted for offence punishable under Sections 16(1)a(i)(ii)/7(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (for brevity 'the Act,
1954') and sentenced to undergo 6 months R.I and fine of Rs.5,000/- with usual default stipulation.
02.

Brief facts of the case are that on 26/03/2010, at about 3.15 pm, Yashwant Sharma, the then inspector during the course of inspection went to Kailash Ice-cream Parlour at Jhabua and introduced himself to the shop keeper.
He enquired about the shop keeper and carried out inspection of the shop in the presence of independent witnesses.
When the license was asked for, the shop keeper Kailash Patidar could not produce the same, thereafter he was given eight days time to produce the same.
During inspection, 3 Kgs., of Ice-cream, 200 packets of Ice-candy and 20 Kgs of sugar along with ice-cream machine and thermocol box were found in the shop for making ice-cream.
Sample of 900 grams of Ice-cream was taken through Form 7, money was paid for it and receipt was also taken after completing necessary formalities.
One part of the sample along with Form 7 was sent to State Food Laboratory, Bhopal and rest of the two samples were sealed and sent to the office of 'Swasth Pradhikari' Jhabua.
Vide the analysis report dated 06/05/2010 of State Food Laboratory, Bhopal, the ice-cream sample was found to be adulterated.

On the basis of said report,
complaint was filed after taking necessary permission.

03. Trial Court, while passing the judgment, convicted the applicant for offence punishable under Sections 16(1)a(i)(ii)/7(i) of 'the Act, 1954' and sentenced to undergo 6 months R.I and fine of Rs.5,000/- with usual default stipulation.
An appeal was filed against the said conviction and sentence, which was dismissed by First Additional Sessions Judge, Jhabua, in Cri.
Appeal No.166/2016 vide judgment dated 02/03/2019

. This judgment is under challenge in the present Kamlesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 2 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118542992/
1 revision petition.

sentences.text: 04. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the impugned order passed by the Courts below are contrary to the law and facts on record.

The Courts below has erred by not appreciating the fact that the public analyst report does not specify the quantity of starch found in the sample which was taken, therefore, it does not indicate that the sample was adulterated or injurious to life.
The Courts below has also erred by ignoring the fact that the applicant has been denied of his valuable right under Section 13(2) of 'the Act, 1954'.
It is further submitted that there are material contradictions and omissions in the statement of complainant and other witness vis -a-vis their Court statement.
Prosecution has miserably failed to produce any material to justify the conviction of the applicant, therefore, he prayed for acquittal of the present applicant.

05. On the other hand learned Public Prosecutor opposes the prayer by contending that after due appreciation of the evidence learned Courts below have found the applicant guilty of the offence hence no interference is called for in the concurrent findings recorded by the Courts below.
06.
I have considered the submissions made on behalf of the parties and perused the material on record.

07. From the perusal of the perusal of the Public analyst report, it is established that the sample of the article was not in accordance to the prescribed standards as per item A.12.02.07 of Appendix-B of Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955, therefore, the sample was found to be adulterated.

After filing the complaint, notice was issued to the applicant under Section 13(2) of 'the Act, 1954' by registered post on his address, which was not returned back unserved, therefore, the Court presumed the service of the said notice to the applicant, hence, it cannot be said that the provisions of Section 13(2) has not been complied with.
The commission of offence is proved on the basis of statement of Food Inspector (P.W.1), which is also corroborated with the documents Ex.P/1 to P/22.
The scope of appreciation of evidence in the revision is very limited, therefore, this Court is of the view that the Courts below have rightly believed the testimony of the prosecution witnesses.

08. In view of the aforesaid and on the basis of the material available on the record, this Court is of the considered opinion that the Courts below have not committed any illegality in convicting the applicant offence punishable under Sections 16(1)a(i)(ii)/7(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

The applicant has been awarded 6 months R.I with a fine of Rs.5,000/- for the aforesaid offence, which is minimum sentence prescribed for the said offence, therefore, no interference is warranted in the sentence passed by the Courts below.
09. Accordingly, the present criminal revision is dismissed.
Certified copy as per Rules.
